MAINE DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION
Augusta, Maine 04333-0017
MAINE STORMWATER MANAGEMENT DESIGN MANUAL Volume III – Technical Design Manual
This May 2016 edition supersedes these manuals
This manual is intended to be a guidance document for the design and implementation of sound technical stormwater management systems
treat the first 1 inch of runoff from impervious surfaces
control the peak flow discharges from the 2, 10 and 25-year 24-hour storms
Stormwater management facilities must be designed to treat the first 1 inch of runoff from impervious surfaces and 0.4 inch from landscaped areas.
familiarity with the Rational Method, SCS TR-20 and SCS TR-55 methodology

Chapter 3 Detention Basins for Flooding Control ... Chapter 6 Infiltration BMPs ... Chapter 7 Filtration BMPs ... Chapter 10 LID Practices and Techniques
An underdrained soil filter must detain and filter a runoff volume equal to 1.0 inch times the subcatchment's impervious area plus 0.4 inch times the subcatchment's landscaped developed area.
A filter basin must drain dry in no less than 24 and no more than 48 hours.
The bottom of the constructed basin, including any underdrain soil filters should be one (1) foot above the seasonal high groundwater table
The soil filter over the gravel underdrain pipe bedding must be at least 18 inches deep
The peak water quality storage depth should not exceed 6 inches over a bioretention basin filter.
Recommended infiltration should be less than 2.41 inches per hour but great enough that one inch of stored precipitation infiltrates in 24 hours (i.e. >0.04 inches per hour).
Provide a long and narrow basin shape, with a minimum 2:1 length to width ratio (3:1 is best).
The target detention time for the treatment volume should be between 24 to 48 hours.
A minimum slope of 2% is considered normal for extensive and simple intensive greening.
The bottom of the underdrained soil filter should be a minimum of 18 inches above the seasonal high groundwater table or bedrock

design_parameters.enrich_notes: WQv sizing uses 1.0 in on impervious and 0.4 in on landscaped/developed pervious area (composite volume, not a single depth). SHWT separation varies by BMP: 12 in (1 ft) for detention basins, bioretention, subsurface sand filters; 18 in minimum for grassed underdrained soil filters. Gravel wetlands target 24–48 h detention for WQ volume. Infiltration design cites <2.41 in/hr and >0.04 in/hr so 1 in drains within 24 h. Pervious surfaces: 8 in min filter layer (infiltration) and 4 in min filter bed (underdrained storage/filtration)—no single storage-depth parameter extracted. Proprietary systems use Maine DEP Appendix B approval letters, not TAPE/NJCAT.
